content_metadata.description: The video explores the significance, history, and astronomical aspects of the Nebra Sky Disk, an ancient bronze-age artifact.

qAndA.answer: The Nebra Sky Disk is a bronze-age artifact that depicts an abstract representation of the sun, the moon, and a constellation of stars.
qAndA.question: What is the Nebra Sky Disk?

qAndA.answer: The Nebra Sky Disk is a 3,600-year-old measuring device.
qAndA.question: How old is the Nebra Sky Disk?

qAndA.answer: It is the oldest known physical representation of astronomical phenomena in the world, and it might be one of the earliest calendars ever conceived.
qAndA.question: What is the significance of the Nebra Sky Disk?

qAndA.answer: The Nebra Sky Disk is now part of UNESCO's Memory of the World Register.
qAndA.question: Where is the Nebra Sky Disk currently located?

qAndA.answer: The accuracy of the angles between the rising and setting points at both summer and winter solstices suggests that the disk might have been used to determine when to crop, and when to harvest.
qAndA.question: What does the accuracy of the angles in the Nebra Sky Disk suggest?

youtube_description:
The disk is widely considered to be “one of the most important archaeological finds of the twentieth century” (an expression claimed by UNESCO when the disk was added, in 2013, to the Memory of the World Register), and one of the most sensational European discoveries of the past decades.

Discover more about this artefact on our website: https://crearac.com/artefacts/nebra-sky-disk/
